spec_match.rationale: Teaches navigator.modelContext, a `handler` member and a navigator.modelContext.tools getter. The spec IDL is document.modelContext ([SecureContext]) with registerTool({name,title,description,inputSchema,outputSchema,execute,annotations}, {signal, exposedTo}), getTools() and executeTool(). The page never calls the real API: with --enable-features=WebMCP on Chromium 157 document.modelContext.getTools() still returned [] after 'registering'.

interactive.rationale: The form builds a schema and a mock registry card plus generated code, but it is a local array only.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature index promises registering tools 'using the navigator.modelContext API ... live, in the browser'. The API name is wrong and nothing live happens even when the flag exposes the real API.

edge_cases.rationale: The mock accepts 'bad name!' (the spec rejects names that are empty, longer than 128 characters, or contain characters outside ASCII alphanumerics and _ - . with InvalidStateError, verified on the real API) and silently replaces duplicates (the spec rejects them with InvalidStateError, verified). An empty description is a silent no-op, and AbortSignal unregistration, annotations and outputSchema are not covered.

references.rationale: Cites chromestatus 5117755740913664 and modelcontextprotocol.io, but not the WebMCP spec (webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp).

conformance.rationale: Every assertion in the feature suite passes vacuously when WebMCP is absent: on default Chromium 157 (no document.modelContext) the suite reads 6/6 PASS, and 'registertool-rejects-tool-without-name' passes only because document.modelContext is undefined (TypeError on property access). Nothing exercises getTools(), executeTool(), name validation, duplicate-name InvalidStateError or AbortSignal unregistration.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Register, add param, delete param, invalid name and a hostile description were exercised at both viewports, with and without the WebMCP flag. Console and network were clean, but a crafted description executed script (see open questions). chrome-devtools-mcp is not available in this environment, so this is NOT DevTools-MCP verification (rule 7b); evidence is Playwright headless Chromium 157.0.8103.78 at 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 touch.

telemetry_health.rationale: The shared /public/demo-telemetry.js is injected (runtime/resource errors would be captured) but the page emits no page-specific assertion or interaction events, and /telemetry/demo/events (Basic auth) was not queried in this pass.

design_system.rationale: Uses CSS variables, but some colours are inline styles, the '● live' badge falsely signals a live API, and controls are not 44px.

accessibility.rationale: The name/description inputs have <label for>, but the 'add param name/type/req?' captions are unassociated <label>s backed by aria-label, the ✕ delete buttons are named only '✕', and registry updates are not announced. Accessibility tree not inspected with chrome-devtools-mcp (unavailable).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No page-level overflow at 360x740, but 8 of 10 controls are under 44px tall.

openQuestions.title: Escape tool name/description/param names before innerHTML
openQuestions.detail: renderRegistry and addParam interpolate user input into innerHTML. Verified on Chromium 157: a description of executed (window.__xss became 1). Build cards with textContent.

openQuestions.title: Register on the real document.modelContext when available
openQuestions.detail: Feature-detect document.modelContext and call registerTool({name, description, inputSchema, execute}, {signal}), then render from await getTools() so the registry is the browser's real one. Show the real InvalidStateError for an invalid or duplicate name and the TypeError for a missing description. Unregister via AbortController. All of this was verified working on Chromium 157 with --enable-features=WebMCP. Keep the mock only as a clearly labelled fallback.

openQuestions.title: Replace origin-trial framing with the real flag steps
openQuestions.detail: ChromeStatus records no origin trial for 5117755740913664 (status 'Proposed', flag 'Experimental Web Platform features' / finch 'WebMCP'). Verified on Chromium 157: document.modelContext appears with --enable-features=WebMCP, --enable-blink-features=WebMCP or --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, and navigator.modelContext is never exposed. Pages variously claim an 'Origin Trial (Chrome 149-156)' token, 'navigator.mcpServer with the WebMCP flag', or a 146 flag. Banner should give chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features, --enable-blink-features=WebMCP and --enable-features=WebMCP, note [SecureContext], and match across all four concepts and the feature index (rule 10).

openQuestions.title: Correct the API names in the generated code and the 'How the API works' block
openQuestions.detail: Use document.modelContext, `execute(input, {signal})` instead of `handler`, and getTools() instead of `.tools`. Mention title, outputSchema and annotations (readOnlyHint, untrustedContentHint, consequentialHint).

openQuestions.title: Flag for a human: WebMCP conformance suite passes vacuously and asserts sync throw for a promise API
openQuestions.detail: Conformance is immutable, so this is a human decision. On Chromium 157 without the flag the suite reads 6/6 PASS with no document.modelContext; the 'throws' assertion for a nameless tool only passes because the property access throws. In the spec registerTool returns a Promise and a missing required dictionary member becomes a rejected promise (verified with the flag: the promise rejects with TypeError), so a synchronous-throw contract is the wrong shape. Additive assertions for getTools()/executeTool(), name-charset InvalidStateError, duplicate-name InvalidStateError and AbortSignal unregistration (all verified behaviourally on Chromium 157 + WebMCP flag) would make the suite meaningful.

openQuestions.title: Add an annotations + AbortSignal lifecycle concept
openQuestions.detail: Register with ToolAnnotations hints, unregister via options.signal, and observe the toolchange event. Verified on Chromium 157 + flag: aborting removes the tool from getTools().

openQuestions.title: Re-verify with chrome-devtools-mcp (Canary + WebMCP flag) and inspect the accessibility tree
openQuestions.detail: This pass used Playwright headless Chromium 157 because chrome-devtools-mcp was unavailable; repeat the control walk, console/network check and accessibility-tree inspection through the MCP per rule 7b.

guidanceConsulted.query: sanitize untrusted HTML with setHTML instead of innerHTML
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Never write untrusted strings into innerHTML sinks; use textContent/DOM construction or a sanitizer/Trusted Types policy.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: user-supplied strings reach innerHTML in this page; recorded as a major open question.

guidanceConsulted.query: form validation error messages for required inputs
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Give clear, accessible error feedback for invalid or missing required input after user interaction.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: invalid input (bad tool name / empty required param / invalid JSON) is silently accepted or ignored; recorded as an open question.

guidanceConsulted.query: live region announcing dynamic log output
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce dynamically changing status/log output through an appropriate live region or <output>, keep native semantics and associated labels for controls.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: the page's changing readouts carry no aria-live/role=status; recorded as an open question.

guidanceConsulted.query: minimum touch target size for buttons on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep touch targets usable (~44px) and content within its space on narrow viewports.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review only: measured controls below 44px tall at 360x740; recorded under mobile_desktop_parity.

summary: A mock tool builder that teaches a non-spec surface (navigator.modelContext, handler, .tools) and never touches the real API, even though Chromium 157 exposes a working document.modelContext behind the WebMCP flag. It accepts names the spec rejects and has a verified script-executing innerHTML sink. Verified with Playwright headless Chromium 157, not chrome-devtools-mcp.
